Record in source catalog DPLA identifier: d49649789513ac633fc9252021db12c4 Columbus Metropolitan Library identifier: HA3_B10_0388.tif
photos.source_description: View of the water tower and Kapellbrücke, or Chapel Bridge, which spans the Reuss River in Lucerne. Constructed in the 14th century, it is is considered Europe's oldest covered bridge. The Arrases visited Lucerne during their 1913 tour of Europe. Note on slide reads "Kapell-Brucke &light house 164 paintings." Edmund F. Arras (7/7/1875-10/19/1951), a prominent Columbus businessman and entrepreneur, founded one of Columbus, Ohio’s first property rental agencies in 1892. Trained as a lawyer, he graduated from OSU law school in 1896 and went on to hold positions in numerous civic groups around the city. He was particularly active within Kiwanis International and was involved with several local religious organizations. In 1913, he and his wife Elizabeth traveled to the World Sunday School Association Convention in Zurich, Switzerland. They continued on to travel extensively throughout Europe documenting their journey through photographs. Due to the timing of their trip, these photos comprise a valuable collection of images of European cities later devastated by war. The Arras family's lantern slides and negatives include images from their 1913 travels through US east coast cities, Atlantic islands of the Azores, Madeira, Gibraltar and the countries of Algeria, Italy, Switzerland, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, France, England, and Ireland. Also included are images from their 1920 train journey from Chicago to the western US for the Kiwanis Convention in Portland. These photographs include images of Chicago, Denver and western National Parks. Glass lantern slide of image also in collection HA3_B03_080.

photos.caption: Stanserhorn CabriO
photos.creator: Dennis G. Jarvis
photos.source_description: The “CabriO” cable car is the world’s first cable car with a roofless upper deck. The comfortable double-decker is the very latest in cable car technology. The lower wall-to-wall windows has space for 60 people. The sun deck, offers room for about 30 people. The guests can enjoy 360° panoramic views as well as the fresh mountain air. The car moves on two side-mounted support cables – a technological innovation.

photos.caption: Tell Monument in Altdorf by night
photos.query: 2019 Tell Monument Statue Telldenkmal Altdorf Uri Switzerland
photos.commons_title: File:2019 Tell Monument Statue (Telldenkmal) Altdorf Uri Switzerland Ank Kumar Infosys Limited 03.jpg
photos.creator: Ank Kumar
photos.source_description: Tell Monument (Telldenkmal) It is a memorial statue to the Swiss legendary folk hero William Tell. It is located in the Centre of the marketplace (Rathausplatz) of Altdorf, Canton Uri , Switzerland. This monument was created by Richard Kissling between 1882 to 1895 as a Neoclassical sculpture. The date 1307 mentioned at the base of the monument refers to the Rütli Oath ((Rütlischwur) : the legendary oath taken at the foundation of the Old Swiss Confederacy in 1307 by the three founding Swiss cantons of Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden. The statue depicts William Tell with an arm resting on his crossbow and the other outstretched holding the arrow that famously shot the apple off his son’s head and thereby saving them from immediate execution by the tyrannical town bailiff, Gessler. The location of the statue is supposedly where William Tell shot the apple for his freedom. The origin of this folk tale is in 'William Tell', a verse drama in five acts by German dramatist Friedrich Schiller, published and produced in 1804 as Wilhelm Tell.
